division: Western Cape - City of Cape Town
name: Teraco CT1 (Rondebosch)
notes: Teraco's original Cape Town facility in Rondebosch, operational since 2009, vendor-neutral colocation and interconnection hub (Carrier Hotel, CAPE-IX co-located); expanded several times. Teraco official Cape Town page confirms CT1/CT2. Exact current MW not publicly stated.

division: Western Cape - City of Cape Town
name: Teraco CT2 (Brackenfell) hyperscale campus
notes: Teraco CT2 at 57 Tiber Road, Brackengate 2, Brackenfell: Phase 1 (~18MW, 20,000 sq m) completed and operational since Oct 2021; Phase 2 (~30MW) expansion targeted Q1 2025 availability, lifting campus critical IT load to ~50MW total per ITWeb/Teraco. Status construction (phase 2) with Phase 1 operational.

division: Western Cape - City of Cape Town
name: Africa Data Centres CPT1 (Diep River / De Waal Road)
notes: ADC Cape Town CPT1 at Diep River/De Waal Road: ~5.5MW original power, R5.5bn expansion added 6MW (~1,000 racks) live by 2024 per official announcement and Business Day; total ~11.5MW+ (some sources cite up to 20MW campus). In May 2025 ADC deployed self-cooling (dry cooling) technology at CPT1 to eliminate water usage (htxt).

division: Western Cape - City of Cape Town
name: Africa Data Centres CPT2 (second Cape Town facility)
notes: ADC announced a second 20MW Cape Town facility with site preparation/construction started (DCD, ITWeb) as part of ADC's $500m pan-African expansion. Trade-press grade B; no operator facility page with address yet.

division: Western Cape - City of Cape Town
name: Equinix Cape Town Campus (King Air Industria, two hyperscale data centres)
notes: Equinix's Cape Town campus at King Air Industria (Pallotti Rd, Matroosfontein, ~30-acre site adjacent to Cape Town International Airport): City of Cape Town Municipal Planning Tribunal approved the land-use/rezoning application on 14 July 2026 for two hyperscale data centres totalling >120,000 sq m, up to ~160MW (per press ~174MW electricity); dry-air cooling confirmed by Equinix. Objections pending: Legal Resources Centre considering appeal (Business Day 2026-07-20), Foxglove/housing-movement challenge (2026-04-29), Engineering News reports King David Golf Club (site owner) and Equinix had 30 days to respond with City 180 days to decide on the environmental challenge. Equinix also announced (Apr 2026, Bloomberg via MarketScreener) ZAR7.5bn ($396m) for 160MW additional SA capacity incl. this campus. Status: land-use approved, not yet environmental/building-approved or under construction - per methodology Cape Town approvals are staged.

division: Western Cape - City of Cape Town

developer: Cavaleros Group / Cosmas Data Cities (CDC), with Knight Frank & Future-tech
notes: Cavaleros Group launched data-centre division Cosmas Data Cities (Nov 2025, DCD): 100-acre/100-hectare Cape Town campus could total 360MW (360MVA available power per Baxtel) to become one of the largest DC availability zones in Sub-Saharan Africa; sister campus at Samrand (Johannesburg, 200MW via 450MW self-built switching station) is in Tshwane division. Status announced/planned; no zoning/EA/building records found yet - early-stage lead per methodology (announced = C/B-).
